In ordinary electromagnetism the four Maxwell equations, in differential form, are  

1. ∇·E = ρ/ε₀  (Gauss for E)  
2. ∇·B = 0    (Gauss for B)  
3. ∇×E = −∂B/∂t (Faraday’s law)  
4. ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t (Ampère–Maxwell)

If real magnetic charges (monopoles) ρ_m and their current J_m exist, we must introduce them in a way that satisfies a magnetic-charge continuity equation  
∂ρ_m/∂t + ∇·J_m = 0.

The minimal, self-consistent and (dually) symmetric way to do that is  

1. ∇·E = ρ/ε₀             (unchanged)  
2. ∇·B = μ₀ρ_m            (has magnetic-charge source)  
3. ∇×E = −μ₀J_m − ∂B/∂t      (has magnetic-current term)  
4. ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t      (unchanged)

So only two of the four equations are altered:

• The divergence (flux) equation for B.  
• The curl (circulation) equation for E.

Thus the changed equations are the ones “related to the circulation of the electric field and the divergence of the magnetic field.”

Answer: B
